title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy option to automatically block identified external bots
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents the blocking option in the feature guide, including its admin-center label and what happens to blocked participants. The briefing incorrectly says these details remain unpublished; importantly, blocked participants are not offered organizer approval in the lobby.

claims.claim: Teams is adding a meeting-policy option to automatically block identified external meeting bots.
claims.quote: Extending the admin controls provided for managing external AI bots and regulating their access to your meetings, we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.claim: The notice describes adding an option to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature guide still documents only two options and does not yet include automatic blocking.
claims.quote: | Block all detected bots | *BlockDetectedBots* | Detected external bots are automatically blocked from joining meetings. They can't be admitted by meeting organizers or other participants. |
claims.fix: Replace every assertion that the feature guide lists only two options with 'The feature guide documents three options: Do not detect bots, When detected, require approval before joining (default), and Block all detected bots.' In the Before rollout bullet, remove the clause claiming the guide lists only two options.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Do not detect bots leaves bots unmarked and subject to normal external-participant access and lobby settings.
claims.quote: Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings and follow the meeting's existing access and lobby settings.

claims.claim: The feature guide calls the disabling-detection value AllowBots.
claims.quote: | Do not detect bots | *AllowBots* |

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference instead lists AllowAllBots for disabling detection.
claims.quote: **AllowAllBots**: Don't detect bots; Bots will appear the same as other participants. Standard lobby policies will apply to them.

claims.claim: RequireApprovalWhenDetected is the existing setting's default value.
claims.quote: **RequireApprovalWhenDetected**: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: Under the approval option, detected bots are identified in the lobby and require admission before joining.
claims.quote: Detected bots are placed in the meeting lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration. Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode BlockDetectedBots configures automatic blocking.
claims.quote: **BlockDetectedBots**: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center route is Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy.
Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: The setting governs meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy, with user or group-level scope.
claims.quote:
The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: Administrators can configure the setting in the default org-wide policy or a targeted policy for particular users or groups.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: The feature guide marks this content as applying to meetings, not events.
claims.quote: **APPLIES TO:**![Image of a checkmark for yes](/en-us/office/media/icons/success-teams.png) Meetings ![Image of a x for no](/en-us/office/media/icons/cancel-teams.png) Events

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting bots can record or transcribe meetings without participants' awareness.
claims.quote: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External bots can store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organization's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: Teams bot detection uses infrastructural and behavioral signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process. We utilize a combination of infrastructural and behavioral signals

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Some bots may evade detection, so blocking detected bots does not guarantee blocking every external bot.
claims.quote: The Block all detected bots option applies to bots identified by Teams detection mechanisms. It does not guarantee that all external bots will be blocked.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Detection can misclassify human participants as bots.
claims.quote: Detection may incorrectly identify a human participant as a bot. How these participants can join depends on the configured policy:

claims.claim: The existing approval experience lets organizers admit a falsely detected person and mark them This is not a bot.
claims.quote: Require approval before joining: Organizers can admit the participant from the lobby and use the This is not a bot option to correct the participant's representation in that meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether blocked participants get a lobby admission route or whether organizers can override blocking.
claims.quote: Detected bots are automatically blocked from joining the meeting. They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval, and meeting organizers can't admit them.
claims.fix: Replace the absence sentence with 'Under Block all detected bots, detected participants are not placed in the lobby for organizer approval and organizers cannot admit them. Where supported, eligible people incorrectly identified as bots can use email verification recovery to verify their identity and attempt to join.' Remove the Open questions bullet asking whether organizers can override blocking, or narrow it to 'What exact message does a blocked participant see?' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots.

claims.claim: The admin-center label for automatic blocking is not yet documented.
claims.quote: | Block all detected bots | *BlockDetectedBots* |
claims.fix: Remove the Open questions bullet asking for the admin-center label: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots documents it as 'Block all detected bots'.
